value.literal: Mao Zilian, Li Sanxi, Kong Jingzong, Li Shikui, Shen Zhang, Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, Kang Gongbi, Zuo Bi, younger brother: Yuan

value.zh: 天會二年，知新城事。
value.en: In the second year of Tianhui he was put in charge of Xincheng.
value.literal: In the second year of Tianhui he was made administrator of Xincheng.

value.zh: 城邑初建，彥倫為經畫，民居、公宇皆有法。
value.en: When the new town was first laid out, Yanlun planned it so that private homes and public buildings alike followed a coherent design.
value.literal: As the town was first being built, Yanlun planned it, and both private dwellings and public offices were all laid out according to rule.

value.zh: 改靜江軍節度留後，知鹹州煙火事。
value.en: He was transferred to military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army and charged with beacon-fire affairs in Xian Prefecture.
value.literal: He was changed to military commissioner designate of the Jingjiang Army and made overseer of beacon-fire affairs in Xian Prefecture.

value.zh: 未幾，遷靜江軍節度使。
value.en: Shortly afterward he was promoted to full military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.
value.literal: Before long he was promoted to military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army.

value.zh: 天眷初，行少府監兼都水使者，充提點京城大內所，改利涉軍節度使。
value.en: At the start of the Tianjuan era he served as acting director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrent commissioner of waterways, supervised the capital's inner-palace establishment, and was then made military commissioner of the Lishe Army.
value.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan he acted as director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrently commissioner of waterways, served as intendant of the capital inner palace office, and was changed to military commissioner of the Lishe Army.

value.zh: 未閱月，還，複為提點大內所。
value.en: Within a month he was back at court and again made intendant of the inner palace office.
value.literal: Within less than a month he returned and again became intendant of the inner palace office.

value.zh: 彥倫性機巧，能迎合悼合意，由是頗見寵用。
value.en: Yanlun was clever by nature and skilled at winning Daohe's favor, and through this he rose to considerable trust and preferment.
value.literal: Yanlun was by nature clever and able to cater to Dao-He's wishes; for this reason he came to be greatly favored and employed.

value.zh: 歲餘，遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，為宋國歲元使。
value.en: A year later he was made commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and sent as the Jin envoy for the Song New Year audience.
value.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to commander-in-chief of the palace guard horse and foot armies and served as Song New Year's envoy.

value.zh: 改禮部尚書，加特進，封郇國公。
value.en: He was appointed minister of rites, granted the extraordinary promotion rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.
value.literal: He was changed to minister of rites, given the extraordinary promotion rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

value.zh: 天德二年，出為大名尹。
value.en: In the second year of Tiande he was posted out as prefect of Daming.
value.literal: In the second year of Tiande he went out as prefect of Daming.

value.zh: 明年，詔彥倫營造燕京宮室，以疾卒，年六十九。
value.en: The following year he was ordered to build the palaces at Yanjing. He died of illness at the age of sixty-nine.
value.literal: The next year an edict ordered Yanlun to construct the palaces at Yanjing; he died of illness, aged sixty-nine.

value.zh: 子璣。
value.en: His son was Ji.
value.literal: His son was Ji.

value.zh: 是時，璣年已七十，詔許朝參得坐於廊下。
value.en: By then Ji was already seventy, and an edict allowed him to take a seat in the corridor when he attended court.
value.literal: At that time Ji was already seventy; an edict permitted him at court audience to be seated in the corridor.

value.zh: 複致仕。
value.en: He retired from office once more.
value.literal: He again retired from office.

value.zh: 泰和初，詔璣天壽節預宴。
value.en: At the start of the Taihe era he was ordered to attend the emperor's birthday banquet.
value.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, an edict summoned Ji to the Tian Shou festival banquet.

value.zh: 二年，元妃李氏生皇子，滿三月，章宗以璣老而康強，命以所策杖為洗兒禮物。
value.en: In the second year, when Primary Consort Li gave birth to a prince and the third month was reached, Zhangzong—seeing that Ji was old but still vigorous—commanded that the walking staff Ji used be presented as the gift for the infant-washing rite.
value.literal: In the second year the primary consort Lady Li bore a prince; when three months were complete, Zhangzong, because Ji was old yet hale, ordered that the staff he leaned on be the gift for the washing-of-the-child ceremony.

value.zh: 章宗幸玉泉山，詔璣與致仕宰相俱會食，許策杖給扶。
value.en: When Zhangzong visited Jade Spring Mountain, he summoned Ji to dine with the retired chief ministers and allowed him a staff and aides to steady him.
value.literal: Zhangzong visited Jade Spring Mountain and ordered Ji and retired chief ministers to dine together, permitting a staff and attendants to support him.

value.zh: 後預天壽節，上命璣與大臣握槊戲，璣獲勝焉。
value.en: On a later birthday celebration the emperor had Ji play shuo, a board game, against the chief ministers, and Ji won.
value.literal: Later he attended the Tian Shou festival; the emperor ordered Ji and the great ministers to play shuo, a board game; Ji won.

value.zh: 從上秋山，賜名馬。
value.en: He accompanied the emperor on the autumn hunt in the hills and was given a fine horse.
value.literal: He followed the emperor to the autumn mountain hunt and was granted a famous horse.

value.zh: 上曰：「酬卿博直。」
value.en: The emperor said, "This repays your blunt honesty at the shuo match."
value.literal: The emperor said: "This rewards your forthright counsel in the shuo match."

value.zh: 其眷遇如此。
value.en: Such was the degree of favor he enjoyed.
value.literal: Such was the favor shown him.

value.zh: 泰和六年卒，年八十。
value.en: He died in the sixth year of Taihe at the age of eighty.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he died, aged eighty.

value.zh: 子亨嗣。
value.en: His son was Hengsi.
value.literal: His son was Hengsi.

value.zh: 亨嗣與弟亨益，盡友愛之道。
value.en: Hengsi and his younger brother Hengyi were models of fraternal devotion.
value.literal: Hengsi and his younger brother Hengyi fully practiced brotherly affection.

value.zh: 亨嗣初以祖廕得官，大定十六年，父璣為同知宣徽院事，當廕子，亨嗣以讓弟亨益。
value.en: Hengsi had first entered office through his grandfather's yin privilege. In the sixteenth year of Dading, when his father Ji became vice director of the Privy Portal Office and was entitled to pass office to a son, Hengsi yielded the privilege to his younger brother Hengyi.
value.literal: Hengsi had first received office through his grandfather's privilege; in the sixteenth year of Dading his father Ji was vice director of the Privy Portal Office and was due a yin privilege for a son; Hengsi yielded it to his younger brother Hengyi.

value.zh: 亨益早卒，子兟。
value.en: Hengyi died young, leaving a son named Shen.
value.literal: Hengyi died young; his son was Shen.

value.zh: 兟幼稚，亨嗣盡以舊業田宅奴畜財物與之。
value.en: Shen was still a child, so Hengsi turned over to him the entire family patrimony—fields, houses, slaves, livestock, and goods.
value.literal: Shen was young; Hengsi gave him all the family's old estates, fields, houses, slaves, livestock, and goods.

value.zh: 璣字正甫，以廕補閤門祗候，累遷客省使，兼東上閤門使，改提點太醫、教坊、司天，充大定十五年宋主生日副使，遷同知宣徽院事。
value.en: Ji, courtesy name Zhengfu, entered service by yin privilege as a privy-gate attendant. He rose through the posts of guest liaison commissioner and concurrent eastern upper privy-gate commissioner, then became intendant of the imperial medical service, music conservatory, and astronomical bureau. He served as deputy envoy for the Song emperor's birthday in the fifteenth year of Dading and was made vice director of the Privy Portal Office.
value.literal: Ji, style Zhengfu, entered office by yin privilege as a privy-gate attendant. He was promoted repeatedly to guest liaison commissioner and concurrently eastern upper privy-gate commissioner, then was changed to intendant of the imperial medical service, music conservatory, and astronomical bureau. He served as deputy envoy for the Song emperor's birthday in the fifteenth year of Dading and was transferred to vice director of the Privy Portal Office.

value.zh: 丁母憂，起複太府監，改開遠軍節度使，入為右宣徽使。
value.en: After mourning his mother he was recalled as director of the Palace Storehouse, then made military commissioner of Kaiyuan Army and entered service as right privy portal commissioner.
value.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, he was recalled to serve as director of the Palace Storehouse, was changed to military commissioner of Kaiyuan Army, and entered service as right privy portal commissioner.

value.zh: 章宗即位，轉左宣徽使，致仕。
value.en: When Zhangzong acceded, he was transferred to left privy portal commissioner and retired.
value.literal: When Zhangzong acceded, he was transferred to left privy portal commissioner and retired from office.

value.zh: 明昌四年，起複左宣徽使，改定武軍節度使，複為左宣徽使。
value.en: In the fourth year of Mingchang he was recalled as left privy portal commissioner, made military commissioner of Dingwu Army, and again appointed left privy portal commissioner.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Mingchang he was recalled as left privy portal commissioner, changed to military commissioner of Dingwu Army, and again made left privy portal commissioner.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 六月戊辰，大赦，增吏位二等。
value.en: The wuchen day in the sixth month brought a general amnesty and a two-grade promotion for every official.
value.literal: In the sixth month, on the wuchen day, a general amnesty; officials’ ranks were increased two grades.

value.zh: 復封賓徒王晏爲吳王。
value.en: Prince Yan of Bintu was restored to the old Wu princedom.
value.literal: Prince Yan of Bintu was again enfeoffed as prince of Wu.

value.zh: 庚午，東萊王蕤、左衛將軍王輿謀廢齊王冏，事泄，蕤廢爲庶人，輿伏誅，夷三族。
value.en: Prince Rui of Donglai and Wang Yu conspired to topple Prince Jiong; when the plot surfaced, Rui was reduced to commoner rank while Wang Yu and three degrees of his kin were executed.
value.literal: On the gengwu day, Prince Rui of Donglai and General of the Left Guards Wang Yu plotted to depose Prince Jiong of Qi; the affair leaked; Rui was deposed to commoner status; Yu submitted to execution; three clans were exterminated.

value.zh: 甲戌，以齊王冏爲大司馬、都督中外諸軍事，成都王穎爲大將軍、錄尚書事，河間王顒爲太尉。
value.en: Prince Jiong became grand marshal and commander-in-chief, Prince Ying general-in-chief with charge of the secretariat, and Prince Yong grand commandant on the jiaxu day.
value.literal: On the jiaxu day, Prince Jiong of Qi was made grand marshal and area commander for all military affairs within and without; Prince Ying of Chengdu was made general-in-chief and recorder of secretariat affairs; Prince Yong of Hejian was made grand commandant.

value.zh: 罷丞相，復置司徒官。
value.en: The chancellorship was abolished and the ministry of education revived.
value.literal: The chancellor was abolished; the office of minister of education was re-established.

value.zh: 己卯，以梁王肜爲太宰，領司徒。
value.en: Prince Rong of Liang was named grand steward while retaining the ministry of education on the jimao day.
value.literal: On the jimao day, Prince Xiong of Liang was made grand steward, concurrently heading the ministry of education.

value.zh: 封齊王冏功臣葛旟牟平公，路季小黃公，衛毅平陰公，劉真安鄉公，韓泰封丘公。
value.en: Prince Jiong of Qi's meritorious followers were enfeoffed: Ge Yu as Duke of Mouping, Lu Ji as Duke of Xiaohuang, Wei Yi as Duke of Pingyin, Liu Zhen as Duke of Anxiang, and Han Tai as Duke of Fengqiu.
value.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi’s meritorious subjects Ge Yu was enfeoffed duke of Mouping, Lu Ji duke of Xiaohuang, Wei Yi duke of Pingyin, Liu Zhen duke of Anxiang, and Han Tai duke of Fengqiu.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
value.en: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
value.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.

value.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！
value.en: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
value.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

value.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
value.en: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.
value.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.

value.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
value.en: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.
value.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.

value.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
value.en: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.
value.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.

value.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
value.en: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
value.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

value.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
value.en: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
value.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

value.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
value.en: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
value.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

value.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
value.en: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
value.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Alas, how grievous!
value.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!

value.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
value.en: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.
value.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.

value.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。
value.en: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.
value.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.

value.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？
value.en: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
value.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

value.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。
value.en: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.
value.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.

value.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
value.en: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.
value.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.

value.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
value.en: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?
value.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!

value.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。
value.en: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
value.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

value.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
value.en: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.
value.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.

value.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。
value.en: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
value.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

value.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。
value.en: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.
value.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.

value.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
value.en: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.
value.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.

value.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。
value.en: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.
value.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.

value.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
value.en: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.
value.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.

value.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
value.en: Courtiers weep together.
value.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!

value.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」
value.en: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."
value.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'

value.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
value.en: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
value.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.

value.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
value.en: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
value.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

value.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
value.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
value.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

value.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
value.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
value.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

value.zh: 梁書卷第十三 列傳第七
value.en: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7
value.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 13, Biographies 7

value.zh: 迹平生之耿介，實有心於獨往。
value.en: The track of my days was straight and hard; I meant to keep a heart that went alone.
value.literal: The traces of my life's upright integrity—truly I kept a heart that walked alone.

value.zh: 思幽人而軫念，望東臯而長想。
value.en: I mourned the man apart from the world and turned my eyes to the eastern terrace in longing.
value.literal: I thought of the reclusive man and felt deep pity; I gazed at the eastern ridge and longed.

value.zh: 本忘情於徇物，徒羈絏於天壤。
value.en: I was born to forget the world's goods, yet only wound in heaven's dust.
value.literal: By nature I had forgotten feeling for outer things, only to be bound by heaven's dust.

value.zh: 應屢歎於牽絲，陸興言於世網。
value.en: Ying Pu-ke groaned at every tug of thread; Lu Ji named the net the age weaves.
value.literal: Ying Pu-ke sighed again and again at threads that pulled; Lu Ji spoke of the world's net.

value.zh: 事滔滔而未合，志悁悁而無爽。
value.en: Business poured on without rest; my heart was tight but never bent.
value.literal: Affairs ran on, ungathered; my will was anxious yet never lost its integrity.

value.zh: 路將殫而彌峭，情薄暮而踰廣。
value.en: The path was nearly spent and grew sharper; at evening my longing widened.
value.literal: The road neared its end and grew steeper still; feeling at dusk spread ever wider.

value.zh: 抱寸心其如蘭，何斯願之浩蕩。
value.en: I carried a span of heart sweet as orchid—how wide this wish runs!
value.literal: I held an inch of heart fragrant as orchids—how vast this longing's flood!

value.zh: 詠歸歟而躑跼，眷岩阿而抵掌。
value.en: I sang of going home yet could not move; I turned to the cliff and struck my palms.
value.literal: I chanted "Returning!" yet stood rooted in place; I looked toward the rocky crags and clapped my hands.

value.zh: 列傳第五十九
value.en: the 59th year of Biography
value.literal: Biographies number fifty-nine

value.zh: 及長，好學，善屬文。
value.en: As an adult he loved learning and wrote with skill.
value.literal: When grown, he loved learning and was skilled at composition.

value.zh: 性沖靜，有棲遁志。
value.en: He was gentle and withdrawn by nature and aspired to a life of seclusion.
value.literal: His nature was mild and still; he had the resolve to dwell in seclusion.

value.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，對策高第。
value.en: At his coming of age he was recommended as Cultivated Talent and placed at the top of the policy examination.
value.literal: At weak cap he was recommended as Cultivated Talent and ranked high in the policy response.

value.zh: 起家梁宣城王國左常侍。
value.en: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the establishment of the Liang Prince of Xuancheng.
value.literal: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the Liang Prince of Xuancheng's establishment.

value.zh: 大同中，嘗驟雨，殿前往往有雜色寶珠，梁武觀之，甚有喜色，寄因上瑞雨頌。
value.en: During the Datong era a sudden rain once left multicolored pearls scattered before the hall. Emperor Wu looked on with delight, and Ji submitted an Ode on the Auspicious Rain.
value.literal: In the Datong era, once during a sudden rain, before the hall there often appeared multicolored precious pearls; Liang Wu viewed them with great pleasure; Ji thereupon submitted an Ode on Auspicious Rain.

value.zh: 帝謂寄兄荔曰：「此頌典裁清拔，卿之士龍也，將如何擢用？」
value.en: The Emperor told Ji's elder brother Li, "This ode is elegant and elevated. He is your Lu Ji—how shall we promote him?"
value.literal: The Emperor said to Ji's elder brother Li: "This ode's style is clear and elevated; he is your Shi Long—how shall we promote and employ him?"

value.zh: 寄聞之歎曰：「美盛德之形容，以申擊壤之情耳，吾豈買名求仕者乎？」
value.en: When Ji heard this he sighed. "I only meant to praise the Emperor's virtue and voice the people's joy. Am I the sort to trade on a name for office?"
value.literal: When Ji heard, he sighed: "To praise the sage virtue's likeness and express the feeling of beating clods—that is all; am I one who buys a name to seek office?"

value.zh: 乃閉門稱疾，唯以書籍自娛。
value.en: He shut his gate, pleaded illness, and amused himself with books alone.
value.literal: He then shut his gate and claimed illness, amusing himself only with books.

value.zh: 岳陽王察為會稽太守，寄為中記室，領郡五官掾。
value.en: When the Prince of Yueyang, Cha, became Administrator of Kuaiji, Ji served as Central Recorder with concurrent duty as Commandery Five-Officials Assistant.
value.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang Cha was Administrator of Kuaiji, Ji was Central Recorder and concurrent Commandery Five-Officials Assistant.

value.zh: 在職簡略煩苛，務存大體，曹局之內，終日寂然。
value.en: In office he cut through petty bureaucracy and kept to essentials. His bureau was silent all day long.
value.literal: In office he simplified what was tedious and exacting, keeping to the great pattern; within the bureau all day was silence.

value.zh: 張昭字子布，彭城人也。
value.en: Zhang Zhao, styled Zibu, hailed from Pengcheng.
value.literal: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Zibu, was a man of Pengcheng.

value.zh: 少好學，善隸書，從白侯子安受《左氏春秋》，博覽眾書，與琅邪趙昱、東海王朗俱發名友善。
value.en: As a youth he loved books, wrote a fine clerical hand, studied the Zuo commentary under Bai Hou Zi’an, read omnivorously, and made his name alongside Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai.
value.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled at clerical script, received Zuo's Spring and Autumn from Bai Hou Zi'an, read widely among texts, and together with Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai rose to fame as friendly associates.

value.zh: 弱冠察孝廉，不就。
value.en: Recommended as filially pious and incorrupt at his capping, he refused appointment.
value.literal: At the capping age he was investigated as filially pious and incorrupt but did not take office.

value.zh: 與朗共論舊君諱事，州裡才士陳琳等皆稱善之。
value.en: He argued with Wang Lang over taboos for former rulers; local talents such as Chen Lin praised his performance.
value.literal: Together with Lang he debated the affair of tabooing former lords; talented men of the commandery such as Chen Lin all praised them.

value.zh: 〈时汝南主簿应劭议宜为旧君讳，论者皆互有异同，事在《风俗通》。
value.en: 〈Ying Shao of Runan had argued for tabooing former masters; the dispute is recorded in the Fengsu tong.)
value.literal: 〈At that time Ying Shao, chief clerk of Runan, argued one ought taboo former lords; debaters differed from one another—the affair is in Fengsu tong.

value.zh: 昭著论曰：“客有见大国之议，士君子之论，云起元建武已来，旧君名讳五十六人，以为后生不得协也。
value.en: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A certain visitor had examined the debates of a great state and the arguments of learned gentlemen. He said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later generations could no longer use names with the same sounds.
value.literal: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A guest had seen the deliberations of a great state and the discussions of gentlemen, and said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty, there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later-born people could not use matching sounds.

value.zh: 取乎经论，譬诸行事，义高辞丽，甚可嘉羡。
value.en: Drawn from canonical gloss and matched to precedent, the rhetoric glows—yet something troubles me.
value.literal: Taking from the classics and commentaries, comparing to deeds performed, the righteousness is lofty and phrases lovely—greatly to be admired.

value.zh: 愚意褊浅，窃有疑焉。
value.en: Forgive a shallow mind—I cannot quite agree.
value.literal: My foolish thought is narrow and shallow—I privately harbor doubt.

value.zh: 盖乾坤剖分，万物定形，肇有父子君臣之经。
value.en: Once heaven and earth divided and creation took shape, the bonds of parent and child, ruler and subject, appeared.
value.literal: In general when Heaven and Earth split apart and the myriad things fixed their forms, there began the constant pattern of father and son, lord and minister.

value.zh: 故圣人顺天之性，制礼尚敬，在三之义，君实食之，在丧之哀，君亲临之，厚莫重焉，恩莫大焉，诚臣子所尊仰，万夫所天恃，焉得而同之哉？
value.en: The sage fashioned ritual from heaven’s nature: lords feed us under the “three that endure”; they mourn with us—nothing outweighs that debt. How can subjects rank them with ordinary kin?
value.literal: Therefore the sage complies with heaven's nature, institutes ritual and esteems reverence; in the duty of the three the lord truly nourishes; in mourning's grief the lord personally attends—the thickness cannot be heavier, the grace cannot be greater—truly what ministers and sons revere and myriad men rely on—how can they be equated?

value.zh: 然亲亲有衰，尊尊有杀，故礼服上不尽高祖，下不尽玄孙。
value.en: Yet kinship weakens by generation and mourning scales down—hence hemp stops short of the fifth grandfather above and the fifth grandson below.
value.literal: Yet intimacy toward kin has degrees of decline; reverence toward superiors has steps of reduction—therefore mourning garments upward do not exhaust great-great-grandfather, downward do not exhaust great-great-grandchild.

value.zh: 又传记四世而缌麻，服之穷也；
value.en: Genealogies say after four generations one wears only thin hemp.
value.literal: Moreover transmitted records: four generations and thin hemp—end of garments;

value.zh: 五世袒免，降杀同姓也；
value.en: After five generations one merely bares head and wrist—the mourning grade fades even within the clan.
value.literal: five generations shed turban and fringe—reduced severity toward same surname;

value.zh: 六世而亲属竭矣。
value.en: By the sixth generation kinship ends.
value.literal: six generations and kinship ties are exhausted.

value.zh: 又曲礼有不逮事之义则不讳，不讳者，盖名之谓，属绝之义，不拘於协，况乃古君五十六哉！
value.en: The Summary of Etiquette also exempts those who never served a lord from tabooing him—that ends obligation to a mere name. If distant kin need not rhyme away syllables, why taboo scores of dead kings?
value.literal: Moreover the Summary of Etiquette has the sense that if one did not succeed to service there is no taboo—no taboo refers to personal names; meaning of severed connection is not bound by harmonizing—how much more fifty-six ancient lords!

value.zh: 邾子会盟，季友来归，不称其名，咸书字者，是时鲁人嘉之也。
value.en: When the Zhu ruler met allies and Jiyou came home, the classic wrote his style, not his name—Lu admired the tact.
value.literal: The lord of Zhu at covenant assembly, Jiyou came to return—his name was not called; all were written with style—at that time the people of Lu praised it.

value.zh: 何解臣子为君父讳乎？
value.en: So why insist clerks taboo every syllable of old patrons?
value.literal: How explain ministers and sons tabooing for lord and father?

value.zh: 周穆王讳满，至定王时有王孙满者，其为大夫，是臣协君也。
value.en: Zhou King Mu banned “Man,” yet under King Ding a minister Wangsun Man served—a subject bore the sovereign’s taboo.
value.literal: King Mu of Zhou tabooed Man; when it reached King Ding there was Wangsun Man who was grand officer—that is a minister harmonizing with his lord.

value.zh: 又厉王讳胡，及庄王之子名胡，其比众多。
value.en: King Li banned “Hu,” yet Zhuang’s son was Hu—examples abound.
value.literal: Moreover King Li tabooed Hu; and among King Zhuang's sons one was named Hu—their parallels are numerous.

value.zh: 夫类事建议，经有明据，传有徵案，然后进攻退守，万无奔北，垂示百世，永无咎失。
value.en: Advice must rest on canonical proof and commentary precedent—otherwise posterity laughs.
value.literal: When grouping affairs and proposing counsel, the classics have clear proofs and the commentaries verifiable cases—then advancing attack or retreating defense never flees north in defeat; displaying for a hundred generations, never failing or missing.

value.zh: 今应劭虽上尊旧君之名，而下无所断齐，犹归之疑云。
value.en: Ying Shao honors old masters’ names yet sets no clear rule below—it stays muddled.
value.literal: Now although Ying Shao upward honors former lords' names, downward he decides nothing uniform—still it returns to doubtful clouds.

value.zh: 曲礼之篇，疑事无质，观省上下，阙义自证，文辞可为，倡而不法，将来何观？
value.en: The Summary of Etiquette passages he cites prove nothing; pretty words without law teach nothing.
value.literal: The Summary of Etiquette chapter—doubtful matters lack substance; observing above and below, missing righteousness proves itself—literary phrasing may be composed, advocated but not lawful—what will the future behold?

value.zh: 言声一放，犹拾瀋也，过辞在前，悔其何追！”〉
value.en: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉
value.literal: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉

value.zh: 刺史陶謙舉茂才，不應，謙以為輕己，遂見拘執。
value.en: Prefect Tao Qian nominated him for office; when Zhang Zhao declined, Tao felt insulted and jailed him.
value.literal: Inspector Tao Qian nominated him outstanding talent; he did not respond—Qian thought he slighted himself and thereupon had him seized.

value.zh: 昱傾身營救，方以得免。
value.en: Zhao Yu spent himself on bail until Zhang Zhao went free.
value.literal: Yu threw himself into arranging rescue—only then did he obtain release.

value.zh: 漢末大亂，徐方士民多避難揚土，昭皆南渡江。
value.en: Late Han turmoil drove Xu refugees south—Zhang Zhao crossed with them.
value.literal: At the end of Han great chaos arose; gentlemen and commoners of Xu region mostly fled calamity to Yang territory—Zhao all crossed the river south.

value.zh: 孫策創業，命昭為長史、撫軍中郎將，升堂拜母，如比肩之舊，文武之事，一以委昭。
value.en: Sun Ce named him chief clerk and general who pacifies the army, treated him like family before Lady Wu, and handed him every civil and military file.
value.literal: When Sun Ce founded the enterprise he appointed Zhao chief clerk and General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the Army, ascended the hall to bow to his mother as with old peers shoulder to shoulder—civil and military affairs he wholly entrusted to Zhao.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：策得昭甚悦，谓曰：“吾方有事四方，以士人贤者上，吾於子不得轻矣。”
value.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun Ce rejoiced: I mean to stride the empire—among scholar-advisers I must honor you.
value.literal: [Wu shu] states: Ce gained Zhao and was very pleased, saying to him: I am about to have affairs in the four quarters—with scholar worthies above I cannot treat you lightly.

value.zh: 乃上为校尉，待以师友之礼。〉
value.en: So he raised him to colonel and courted him as mentor.
value.literal: Thereupon he promoted him to colonel and treated him with the ritual of teacher and friend.

value.zh: 昭每得北方士大夫書疏，專歸美於昭，昭欲嘿而不宣則懼有私，宣之則恐非宜，進退不安。
value.en: Northern letters flattered Zhang Zhao alone; silence seemed sneaky, publication awkward—he squirmed either way.
value.literal: Whenever Zhao obtained letters from northern gentlemen-officials they exclusively attributed praise to Zhao; Zhao wished to keep silent and not announce yet feared there was partiality; announcing yet feared it was not appropriate—advancing and retreating were uneasy.

value.zh: 策聞之，歡笑曰："昔管仲相齊，一則仲父，二則仲父，而桓公為霸者宗。
value.en: Sun Ce laughed: Guan Zhong called Huan Gong Father twice—and Huan became hegemon.
value.literal: When Ce heard it he laughed happily and said: Formerly Guan Zhong served Qi—first 'Father Zhong,' second 'Father Zhong,' yet Duke Huan became hegemon-in-chief.

value.zh: 今子布賢，我能用之，其功名獨不在我乎!"，
value.en: Zibu is worthy; if I use him well, the glory is surely mine!
value.literal: Now Zibu is worthy—if I can employ him, will the merit and fame alone not rest with me!"

value.zh: 邵字孝則，博覽書傳，好樂人倫。
value.en: Gu Shao, styled Xiaze, read widely and loved ethics.
value.literal: Shao courtesy name Xiaze—read widely books and transmissions—loved delighting in human relations.

value.zh: 少與舅陸績齊名，而陸遜、張敦、卜靜等皆亞焉。
value.en: As a youth he rivaled uncle Lu Ji; Lu Xun, Zhang Dun, and Bu Jing stood slightly below.
value.literal: Young together with maternal uncle Lu Ji equally famed—yet Lu Xun, Zhang Dun, Bu Jing and others all ranked below.

value.zh: 〈吴录曰：敦字叔方，静字玄风，并吴郡人。
value.en: 〈The Wu lu: Zhang Dun styled Shufang; Bu Jing styled Xuanfeng—both from Wu.)
value.literal: 〈Wu lu states: Dun courtesy name Shufang—Jing courtesy name Xuanfeng—both men of Wu commandery.

value.zh: 敦德量渊懿，清虚淡泊，又善文辞。
value.en: Zhang Dun was deep, quiet, and literary.
value.literal: Dun's virtue capacity deep profound—pure empty bland pale—also skilled literary phrasing.

value.zh: 孙权为车骑将军，辟西曹掾，转主簿，出补海昬令，甚有惠化，年三十二卒。
value.en: Sun Quan named him aide and Haihun magistrate; he died at thirty-two.
value.literal: Sun Quan was chariots-and-cavalry general—summoned western bureau aide—transferred chief clerk—went out supplementing Haihun magistrate—had very benevolent transformation—age thirty-two died.

value.zh: 卜静终於剡令。〉
value.en: Bu Jing died as magistrate of Yan.〉
value.literal: Bu Jing ended at Yan magistrate.〉

value.zh: 自州郡庶幾及四方人士，往來相見，或言議而去，或結厚而別，風聲流聞，遠近稱之。
value.en: Scholars everywhere sought him out and praised his name.
value.literal: From commandery near-worthy and four quarters gentlemen—coming going mutually seeing—some spoke deliberation then left—some tied thick then parted—wind sound flowing heard—far and near praised him.

value.zh: 權妻以策女。
value.en: Sun Quan married him to Sun Ce's daughter.
value.literal: Quan married him to Ce's daughter.

value.zh: 年二十七，起家為豫章太守。
value.en: At twenty-seven he became Yuzhang prefect.
value.literal: Age twenty-seven—rose from house as Administrator of Yuzhang.

value.zh: 下車祀先賢徐孺子之墓。
value.en: On arrival he sacrificed at Xu Ruzi's grave.
value.literal: Descending cart sacrificed to former worthy Xu Ruzi's tomb.

value.zh: 優待其後。
value.en: He cared for Xu's descendants.
value.literal: Generously treated his posterity.

value.zh: 禁其淫祀非禮之祭者。
value.en: He banned illicit shrines.
value.literal: Forbidden those excessive sacrifices not ritual sacrifices.

value.zh: 小吏資質佳者，輒令就學，擇其先進，擢置右職，舉善以教，風化大行。
value.en: He sent promising clerks to school, promoted the best, and spread decorum.
value.literal: Petty clerks with fine capacity—always ordered attend study—selected their advanced—promoted placed right offices—raising good to teach—custom transformation greatly practiced.

value.zh: 初，錢唐丁諝出於役伍，陽羨張秉生於庶民。
value.en: He lifted Ding Xu from the ranks and Zhang Bing from commoners.
value.literal: At first Qiantang Ding Xu emerged from labor ranks—Yangxian Zhang Bing born among common people.

value.zh: 烏程吳粲、雲陽殷禮起乎微賤，邵皆拔而友之，為立聲譽。
value.en: He befriended Wu Can and Yin Li from humble roots.
value.literal: Wucheng Wu Can—Yunyang Yin Li rose from slight mean—Shao all pulled and befriended them—establishing fame reputation.

value.zh: 秉遭大喪，親為制服結絰。
value.en: When Zhang Bing mourned, Gu Shao wore hemp for him.
value.literal: Bing encountered great mourning—personally for him made mourning garments tied headbands.

value.zh: 邵當之豫章，發在近路，值秉疾病，時送者百數。
value.en: Leaving for Yuzhang near home, Zhang Bing fell ill—hundreds came to see him off.
value.literal: When Shao went to Yuzhang—departure on near road—happened Bing illness—at time senders hundred count.

value.zh: 邵辭賓客曰："張仲節有疾，苦不能來別，恨不見之，暫還與訣，諸君少時相待。
value.en: Gu Shao told guests: "Zhang Bing is too sick to say goodbye—I must see him—wait here briefly."
value.literal: Shao dismissed guests saying: "Zhang Zhongjie is ill—bitterly cannot come bid farewell—regrets not seeing him—temporarily return to bid farewell—gentlemen wait a short while."

value.zh: "其留心下士，惟善所在，皆此類也。
value.en: He fussed over humble clients like this.
value.literal: His mind attentive to inferiors—only where good lies—all this kind.

value.zh: 諝至典軍中郎，秉雲陽太守，禮零陵太守，
value.en: Ding Xu rose to colonel of the household army; Zhang Bing and Yin Li became prefects.
value.literal: Xu reached Colonel of the Household Who Commands the Army—Bing Administrator of Yunyang—Li Administrator of Lingling—

value.zh: 〈礼子基作通语曰：礼字德嗣，弱不好弄，潜识过人。
value.en: 〈Yin Li's son Yin Ji wrote Tongyu: Yin Li, styled Desi, was grave even as a boy.)
value.literal: 〈Li's son Ji authored Tongyu stating: Li courtesy name Desi—in youth did not play fondly—latent insight surpassed others.

value.zh: 少为郡吏，年十九，守吴县丞。
value.en: At nineteen he was assistant magistrate of Wu.
value.literal: Young became commandery clerk—age nineteen—acting Wu county assistant.

value.zh: 孙权为王，召除郎中。
value.en: Sun Quan as king named him gentleman of the palace.
value.literal: When Sun Quan became king—summoned removed Gentleman of the Palace.

value.zh: 后与张温俱使蜀，诸葛亮甚称叹之。
value.en: Later he joined Zhang Wen's mission to Shu and impressed Zhuge Liang.
value.literal: Later together with Zhang Wen both went as envoy to Shu—Zhuge Liang greatly praised him.

value.zh: 稍迁至零陵太守，卒官。
value.en: He rose to Lingling prefect and died in harness.
value.literal: Gradually promoted reached Lingling prefect—died in office.

value.zh: 文士传曰：礼子基，无难督，以才学知名，著通语数十篇。
value.en: (Wenshi zhuan: Yin Ji commanded the Feathered Forest and wrote Tongyu.)
value.literal: Wenshi zhuan states: Li's son Ji—Colonel Who Has No Difficulty—by talent and learning became known—composed Tongyu several tens of chapters.

value.zh: 有三子。
value.en: He had three sons.
value.literal: Had three sons.

value.zh: 巨字元大，有才器，初为吴偏将军，统家部曲，城夏口，吴平后，为苍梧太守。
value.en: Eldest Yin Ju became general and Cangwu prefect after Jin conquered Wu.
value.literal: Ju courtesy name Yuanda—had talent and capacity—first was Wu partial general—commanding household command—fortified Xiakou—after Wu pacified—became Cangwu prefect.

value.zh: 少子祐，字庆元，吴郡太守。〉
value.en: Youngest Yin You was Wu prefect.〉
value.literal: Youngest son You—courtesy name Qingyuan—Wu commandery prefect.〉

value.zh: 粲太子少傅。
value.en: Wu Can rose to junior tutor to the heir.
value.literal: Can junior tutor to heir apparent.

value.zh: 世以邵為知人。
value.en: His generation called Gu Shao a judge of character.
value.literal: The age considered Shao as knowing men.

value.zh: 在郡五年，卒官，子譚、承雲。
value.en: After five years as prefect he died; sons Gu Tan and Gu Cheng survived.
value.literal: In commandery five years—died in office—sons Tan and Cheng cloud.

value.zh: 虞翻字仲翔，會稽餘姚人也。
value.en: Yu Fan, styled Zhongxiang, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.
value.literal: Yu Fan, courtesy name Zhongxiang, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻少好学，有高气。
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu records that as a young man Yu Fan loved scholarship and carried himself with uncommon elevation.
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: In youth Fan loved learning and bore himself with lofty pride.

value.zh: 年十二，客有候其兄者，不过翻，翻追与书曰：“仆闻虎魄不取腐芥，磁石不受曲针，过而不存，不亦宜乎！”
value.en: When he was twelve, a visitor called on his brother but snubbed Yu Fan; Fan sent a letter after him: "They say amber ignores rotten mustard and a lodestone spurns a crooked needle—a slight delivered and unnoticed sits ill with neither party."
value.literal: At age twelve a guest came to call on his elder brother but passed by without stopping for Fan; Fan pursued him with a letter saying: "I have heard that amber does not pick up rotten mustard and the lodestone does not take a bent needle; to pass by and pay no heed—is that not fitting!"

value.zh: 客得书奇之，由是见称。〉
value.en: The guest read the note with admiration, and Fan's reputation began from that hour.〉
value.literal: When the guest received the letter he marveled at it, and from this Fan was praised.〉

value.zh: 太守王朗命為功曹。
value.en: The Administrator Wang Lang named him Clerk of Merit.
value.literal: Administrator Wang Lang appointed him Clerk of Merit.

value.zh: 孫策征會稽，翻時遭父喪，衰絰詣府門，朗欲就之，翻乃脫衰入見，勸朗避策。
value.en: While Sun Ce was marching on Kuaiji, Yu Fan was in mourning for his father; he appeared at the yamen gate in sackcloth. Wang Lang meant to comfort him, but Fan stripped the mourning garb, went inside, and urged Lang to withdraw rather than face Ce.
value.literal: Sun Ce campaigned against Kuaiji; Fan was then mourning his father and came to the administrator's gate in mourning dress with hemp cord. Lang wished to approach him, but Fan removed his mourning garments and entered to see him, urging Lang to avoid Ce.

value.zh: 朗不能用。
value.en: Lang would not follow his counsel.
value.literal: Lang could not employ him.

value.zh: 拒戰敗績，亡走浮海。
value.en: He fought and was routed, then fled by ship onto the open sea.
value.literal: He resisted in battle and suffered defeat, then fled and went out to sea.

value.zh: 翻追隨營護，到東部候官，候官長閉城不受，翻往說之，然後見納。
value.en: Fan stayed with the column as escort until they reached Houguan in the eastern circuit; the county magistrate barred the gates until Fan talked him round and won them entry.
value.literal: Fan followed to guard the camp; they reached Houguan in the eastern division. The chief of Houguan closed the city and would not receive them; Fan went and persuaded him, and only then were they admitted.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻始欲送朗到广陵，朗惑王方平记，言“疾来邀我，南岳相求”，故遂南行。
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu adds that Fan first meant to see Wang Lang safely to Guangling, "but Lang trusted an inscription attributed to Wang Fangping—Hasten and summon me; the Southern Peak calls—and turned his course southward instead."
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Fan had first wished to escort Lang to Guangling; Lang was misled by Wang Fangping's inscription, which said Come swiftly and invite me; the Southern Marchmount seeks me, "and therefore went south."

value.zh: 既至候官，又欲投交州，翻谏朗曰：“此妄书耳，交州无南岳，安所投乎？”
value.en: At Houguan he planned to bolt for Jiaozhou; Fan warned him: "That text is nonsense—there is no Southern Marchmount in Jiaozhou; what harbor could such a sign point to?"
value.literal: After reaching Houguan he wished again to flee to Jiaozhou. Fan remonstrated with Lang: "This is a false inscription; Jiaozhou has no Southern Marchmount—where would you go?"

value.zh: 乃止。〉
value.en: Lang gave up the idea.
value.literal: Thereupon he stopped.

value.zh: 朗謂翻曰："卿有老母，可以還矣。"
value.en: Lang told him: "You have an old mother at home—you should go back."
value.literal: Lang said to Fan: "You have an aged mother; you may return."

value.zh: 〈翻别传曰：朗使翻见豫章太守华歆，图起义兵。
value.en: 〈Yu Fan's separate biography says Wang Lang dispatched him to Yuzhang's Hua Xin to plan raising loyal troops.
value.literal: 〈The Separate Biography of Fan states: Lang sent Fan to see Administrator Hua Xin of Yuzhang, plotting to raise troops in righteous revolt.

value.zh: 翻未至豫章，闻孙策向会稽，翻乃还。
value.en: Before he reached Yuzhang he learned Sun Ce was bearing down on Kuaiji and wheeled about.
value.literal: Before Fan reached Yuzhang he heard that Sun Ce was heading for Kuaiji, and Fan then returned.

value.zh: 会遭父丧，以臣使有节，不敢过家，星行追朗至候官。
value.en: His father had just died, yet as an accredited envoy he would not detour home; he marched nights until he caught Wang Lang at Houguan.
value.literal: It happened that he was in mourning for his father; as an envoy under orders he dared not pass his home, but traveled by night and overtook Lang at Houguan.

value.zh: 朗遣翻还，然后奔丧。
value.en: Lang released him to return, and only then could Fan observe the funeral rites.
value.literal: Lang sent Fan back, and only then did Fan go to mourn.

value.zh: 而传云孙策之来，翻衰绖诣府门，劝朗避策，则为大异。〉
value.en: The main narrative, however, claims that when Ce approached, Fan appeared at the yamen in mourning bands urging Lang to yield—quite another story.〉
value.literal: Yet the biography says that when Ce came, Fan in mourning dress went to the gate and urged Lang to avoid Ce—this is a great discrepancy.〉

value.zh: 翻既歸，策覆命為功曹，待以交友之禮。
value.en: Once Fan was back, Sun Ce restored him as Clerk of Merit and courted him as an equal.
value.literal: After Fan returned, Ce again appointed him Clerk of Merit and treated him with the courtesy due a friend.

value.zh: 身詣翻第。
value.en: He called at Fan's house himself.
value.literal: He went in person to Fan's residence.

value.zh: 〈江表传曰：策书谓翻曰：“今日之事，当与卿共之，勿谓孙策作郡吏相待也。”〉
value.en: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan records Ce's letter: "What we face now we shoulder together—do not imagine I would handle you like any county clerk."〉
value.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce wrote to Fan: "Today's affair I must share with you; do not think Sun Ce means to treat you as a mere clerk of the commandery."〉

value.zh: 陸績字公紀，吳郡吳人也。
value.en: Lu Ji, styled Gongji, hailed from Wu commandery.
value.literal: Lu Ji, courtesy name Gongji, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.

value.zh: 父康，漢末為廬江太守。
value.en: His father Kang governed Lujiang in Han's twilight.
value.literal: His father Kang was Administrator of Lujiang at the end of Han.

value.zh: 〈谢承后汉书曰：康字季宁，少惇孝悌，勤脩操行，太守李肃察孝廉。
value.en: 〈Xie Cheng's Hou Hanshu says Kang, styled Jining, earned a Flourishing Talent nomination for filial conduct.
value.literal: 〈Xie Cheng's Later Han History states: Kang, courtesy name Jining, in youth was steeped in filial piety and fraternal duty, diligently cultivated conduct; Administrator Li Su nominated him Flourishing Talent.

value.zh: 肃后坐事伏法，康敛尸送丧还颍川，行服，礼终，举茂才，历三郡太守，所在称治，后拜庐江太守。〉
value.en: When Li Su fell to the law Kang bore his body home, mourned fully, then rose through three prefectures to Lujiang.〉
value.literal: Later Su was executed for an affair; Kang gathered the corpse and escorted the funeral to Yingchuan, observed mourning, finished the rites, was nominated Flourishing Talent, served as Administrator of three commanderies—each place praised his governance—and finally was appointed Administrator of Lujiang.〉

value.zh: 績年六歲，於九江見袁術。
value.en: Ji met Yuan Shu in Jiujiang at age six.
value.literal: At six sui Ji met Yuan Shu on the Jiujiang road.

value.zh: 術出橘，績懷三枚，去，拜辭墮地，術謂曰：“陸郎作賓客而懷橘乎？”
value.en: "Shu offered oranges; six-year-old Ji hid three in his sleeve until they spilled at leave-taking—Shu teased him about stealing fruit."
value.literal: Shu produced oranges; Ji tucked three in his robe; leaving, he bowed in farewell and they fell to the ground; Shu said: "Young Lu, you pocket oranges while a guest?"

value.zh: 績跪答曰："欲歸遺母。
value.en: Ji knelt and said he meant them for his mother.
value.literal: Ji knelt and answered: "I wished to take them home for my mother."

value.zh: "術大奇之。
value.en: Shu stared in delight.
value.literal: Shu greatly marveled at him.

value.zh: 孫策在吳，張昭、張紘、秦松為上賓，共論四海未泰，須當用武治而平之，績年少末坐，遙大聲言曰："昔管夷吾相齊桓公，九合諸候，一匡天下，不用兵車。
value.en: At Ce's council on conquering the realm, boy Ji barked from the lowest seat that Guan Zhong unified Qi without war.
value.literal: When Sun Ce held Wu, Zhang Zhao, Zhang Hong, and Qin Song were chief guests; jointly debating that the four seas were not yet tranquil and arms must rule them, Ji—youngest, seated last—called loudly across the room: "Long ago Guan Zhong ministered Duke Huan of Qi—nine leagues of lords, one restoration under Heaven—without chariot warfare.

value.zh: 孔子曰：'遠人不服，則修文德以來之。
value.en: He quoted Confucius—win strangers with culture, not steel.
value.literal: Confucius said: 'When distant folk do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them.'

value.zh: '今論者不務道德懷取之術，而惟尚武，績雖童蒙，竊所未安也。
value.en: He pleaded his youth yet insisted glorifying arms unsettled him.
value.literal: ' Those who debate today do not labor at virtue and winning hearts but honor force alone—though Ji is a child, privately he cannot rest easy."

value.zh: "昭等異焉。
value.en: The elders listened slack-jawed.
value.literal: Zhao and the others wondered at him.

value.zh: 績容貌雄壯，博學多識，星歷算數無不該覽。
value.en: Strapping and encyclopedic, he mastered stars, calendars, and mathematics.
value.literal: Ji's bearing was heroic and robust; broadly learned and widely informed—astronomy, calendars, reckoning—nothing he failed to survey.

value.zh: 虞翻舊齒名盛，龐統荊州令士，年亦差長，皆與績友善。
value.en: Yu Fan and Pang Tong, his elders in fame, counted Ji friend.
value.literal: Yu Fan by seniority bore famous weight; Pang Tong was Wu's celebrated scholar of Jingzhou; both were somewhat older—all befriended Ji.

value.zh: 孫權統事，闢為奏曹掾，以直道見憚，出為鬱林太守，加偏將軍，給兵二千人。
value.en: Quan named him memorial clerk until blunt honesty exiled him to Yulin with rank and two thousand soldiers.
value.literal: When Sun Quan took charge he summoned Ji as Clerk of Memorial Pillar—straight speaking made men wary—so he went out as Administrator of Yulin with concurrent Lieutenant General and an allotment of two thousand troops.

value.zh: 績既有躄疾，又意在儒雅，非其志也。
value.en: Lame and bookish, generalship never suited him.
value.literal: Ji already suffered lameness and his heart lay with scholar refinement—not his aspiration.

value.zh: 雖有軍事，著述不廢，作《渾天圖》，注《易》釋《玄》，皆傳於世。
value.en: Camp life never stopped his brush—his cosmograph and Change commentary survive.
value.literal: Though military duties pressed he never ceased writing—he composed the Chart of the Encompassing Heavens, annotated the Changes and expounded the Mystery—all handed down.

value.zh: 豫自知亡日，乃為辭曰："有漢志士吳郡陸績，幼敦《詩》、《書》，長玩《禮》、《易》受命南征，遘疾遇厄，遭命不幸，嗚呼悲隔！
value.en: Knowing the hour of death he drafted his lament—a scholar's epitaph for a Han heart broken on the Ling frontier.
value.literal: Yu foreknew his death-day and composed a elegy: "There was a Han loyalist, Lu Ji of Wu commandery—child steeped in Odes and Documents, grown adept at Rites and Changes—received mandate on southern campaign, met illness and hardship, Heaven's lot unkind—alas, sorrow sunders!"

value.zh: "又曰："從今已去，六十年之外，車同軌，書同文，恨不及見也。
value.en: He prophesied reunification within sixty years he would not live to witness.
value.literal: He added: "From now beyond sixty years carts will share gauge and script share form—I regret I shall not see it."

value.zh: "年三十二卒。
value.en: He died at thirty-two.
value.literal: He died at thirty-two sui.

value.zh: 長子宏，會稽南部都尉，次子睿，長水校尉。
value.en: Hong commanded southern Kuaiji; Rui led the Long River corps.
value.literal: Eldest son Hong, Commandant of South Kuaiji; second son Rui, Colonel of Long Rivers.

value.zh: 绩於鬱林所生女，名曰鬱生，適张温弟白。
value.en: His Yulin daughter Yusheng wed Zhang Bai, Zhang Wen's brother.
value.literal: The daughter Ji fathered at Yulin was named Yusheng; she married Zhang Wen's younger brother Bai.

value.zh: 姚信集有表称之曰：“臣闻唐、虞之政，举善而教，旌德擢异，三王所先，是以忠臣烈士，显名国朝，淑妇贞女，表迹家闾。
value.en: "Yao Xin petitioned that Tang-Yu governance honored worthy women as much as loyal men.
value.literal: Yao Xin's collected works preserve a memorial praising her: "Your servant has heard that Tang and Yu's government raised the good and instructed them, hoisted virtue and lifted the unusual—the Three Kings placed this first—therefore loyal ministers and steadfast martyrs shine in court annals, virtuous wives and chaste women leave traces in hamlet gates.

value.zh: 盖所以阐崇化业，广殖清风，使苟有令性，幽明俱著，苟怀懿姿，士女同荣。
value.en: Such praise steadies custom for men and women alike.
value.literal: That widens transformative enterprise and plants pure wind abroad so whoever carries fine nature shows it in light or shade; whoever harbors excellence shares glory between gentlemen and ladies.

value.zh: 故王蠋建寒松之节而齐王表其里，义姑立殊绝之操而鲁侯高其门。
value.en: Classic exemplars—Wang Zhuo's lane, the Lu aunt's gate—prove the point.
value.literal: Hence Wang Zhuo set frost-pine integrity and the Qi king inscribed his lane; the righteous aunt forged unmatched resolve and the Lu marquis raised her gate.

value.zh: 臣切见故郁林太守陆绩女子郁生，少履贞特之行，幼立匪石之节，年始十三，適同郡张白。
value.en: The memorial names Yusheng, Lu Ji's girl—betrothed at thirteen to Zhang Bai.
value.literal: Your servant has personally seen Yusheng, daughter of late Administrator Lu Ji of Yulin—she walked chaste singularity in youth, erected unyielding resolve like undriftable stone; at thirteen sui she married Bai of the same commandery.

value.zh: 侍庙三月，妇礼未卒，白遭罹家祸，迁死异郡。
value.en: Three months into marriage Bai died afar in family disaster.
value.literal: Three months attending the ancestral shrine—wife's rites unfinished—Bai suffered household calamity and died removed to another commandery.

value.zh: 郁生抗声昭节，义形於色，冠盖交横，誓而不许，奉白姊妹嶮巇之中，蹈履水火，志怀霜雪，义心固於金石，体信贯於神明，送终以礼，邦士慕则。
value.en: She refused every suitor, nursed Bai's sisters through ruin, and buried him—Wu's matrons took note.
value.literal: Yusheng raised voice declaring her vow; righteousness shaped her face; coaches crossed pleading remarriage yet she swore refusal; she upheld Bai's sisters through peril, treading flood and fire—mind frost-bright, faith harder than metal or stone, spirit-trust piercing gods—she buried him by ritual so commandery gentlemen took her model.

value.zh: 臣闻昭德以行，显行以爵，苟非名爵，则劝善不严，故士之有诔，鲁人志其勇，杞妇见书，齐人哀其哭。
value.en: The memorial cites Lu dirges and Qi's weeping widow—honor needs a title.
value.literal: Your servant has heard virtue is proclaimed through conduct and conduct displayed through rank—without title or rank encouragement lacks sternness—therefore gentlemen receive dirges: Lu chronicled courage; the Ji wife entered texts and Qi mourned her cry.

value.zh: 乞蒙圣朝，斟酌前训，上开天聪，下垂坤厚，褒郁生以义姑之号，以厉两髦之节，则皇风穆暢，士女改视矣。”
value.en: Yao begged the throne to name Yusheng Righteous Aunt and shame faint hearts."
value.literal: Pray the sacred court weigh ancient precedent—open Heaven's hearing, extend Earth's generosity—award Yusheng the style Righteous Aunt to stiffen young widows' resolve—then royal wind flows serene and gentlemen and ladies revise their gaze."

value.zh: 評曰：虞翻古之狂直，因難免乎末世，然權不能容，非曠宇也。
value.en: Chen Shou calls Fan a classical blunt loyalist ill-suited to a fallen age—yet Quan's inability to shelter him betrays a petty court.
value.literal: The appraisal states: Yu Fan was blunt straightness in the ancient mold—thereby hard to escape harm in a degenerate age—yet that Quan could not tolerate him shows no spacious breadth.

value.zh: 陸績之於揚《玄》，是仲尼之左丘明，老聘之嚴周矣；
value.en: Lu Ji stood to Yang Xiong's Taixuan as Confucius to Zuo Qiu or Laozi to Zhuang Zhou—a peer interpreter.
value.literal: Lu Ji toward Yang Xiong's Mystery parallels Confucius having Zuo Qiuming and Laozi having Zhuang Zhou.

value.zh: 以瑚璉之器，而作守南越，不亦賊夫人歟！
value.en: Temple-grade talent parked on a Ling frontier—what misuse of a man!
value.literal: With talents fit for ritual vessels—yet made guardian of southern Yue—is it not wasting the man!

value.zh: 張溫才藻俊茂，而智防未備，用致艱患。
value.en: Zhang Wen blazed with letters but lacked political guardrails—and paid for it.
value.literal: Zhang Wen's literary brilliance flourished lush—yet wisdom's defenses were not prepared—thereby inviting bitter calamity.

value.zh: 駱統抗明大義，辭切理至，值權方閉不開。
value.en: Luo Tong framed the grand moral case with knife-edge clarity—against Quan's deaf door.
value.literal: Luo Tong upheld and clarified great righteousness—speech cutting, principle utmost—yet met Quan sealed shut and unopening.

value.zh: 陸瑁篤義規諫，君子有稱焉。
value.en: Lu Mao's loyal counsel earned gentlemen's praise.
value.literal: Lu Mao was steadfast in righteousness and remonstrance—gentlemen have praised him for it.

value.zh: 吾粲、朱據遭罹屯蹇，以正喪身，悲夫！
value.en: Wu Can and Zhu Ju died for doing right—grief on grief.
value.literal: Wu Can and Zhu Ju encountered hardship and obstruction—through upright principle lost their lives—alas!

value.zh: 志第十三 天文一
value.en: Treatise Thirteen: Astronomy, Part One
value.literal: Treatise 13: Astronomy 1

value.zh: 漢末吳人陸績善天文，始推渾天意。
value.en: Near the end of Han, Lu Ji of Wu, an expert in astronomy, was the first to work out the Huntian theory in full.
value.literal: At the end of Han, Lu Ji of Wu was skilled in astronomy and was the first to develop the meaning of Huntian.

value.zh: 王蕃者，盧江人，吳時為中常侍，善數術，傳劉洪《乾象曆》。
value.en: Wang Fan came from Lujiang; under Wu he served as Regular Palace Attendant, excelled in mathematical astronomy, and carried on Liu Hong's Supernal Signs Calendar.
value.literal: Wang Fan was a man of Lujiang; in Wu times he served as Regular Palace Attendant, was skilled in numerology, and transmitted Liu Hong's Supernal Signs Calendar.

value.zh: 依《乾象法》而制渾儀，立論考度曰：
value.en: On the Supernal Signs method he built an armillary sphere and drafted a treatise on measurement that begins:
value.literal: Following the method of the Supernal Signs, he made a armillary sphere and set forth a treatise on measurement, saying:

value.zh: 三光之行，不必有常，術家以算求之，各有同異，故諸家曆法參差不齊。
value.en: Sun, moon, and stars do not move by fixed rules; mathematicians derive their paths by calculation, and schools disagree—hence calendars diverge.
value.literal: The motion of the three luminaries is not necessarily constant; numerologists calculate them by computation, each with agreements and differences—hence the calendrical methods of the various schools are uneven and do not align.

value.zh: 《洛書甄耀度》、《春秋考異郵》皆云周天一百七萬一千里，一度為二千九百三十二里七十一步二尺七寸四分四百八十七分分之三百六十二。
value.en: The Radiance of Degrees and the Examination of Strange Correspondences both give Heaven's circuit as 1,071,000 li and one degree as 2,932 li plus 71 paces, 2 chi, 7 cun, 4 fen, and 362/487 of a fen.
value.literal: The Luo shu Radiance of Degrees and Spring and Autumn Examination of Strange Correspondences both say the circuit of Heaven is 1,071,000 li; one degree is 2,932 li, 71 bu, 2 chi, 7 cun, 4 fen, and 362 parts in 487 fen.

value.zh: 陸績云：天東西南北徑三十五萬七千里，此言周三徑一也。
value.en: Lu Ji held that Heaven's diameter is 357,000 li, assuming the classic ratio of circumference three to diameter one.
value.literal: Lu Ji said: Heaven's diameter east-west and north-south is 357,000 li—this speaks of circumference three, diameter one.

value.zh: 考之徑一不啻周三，率周百四十二而徑四十五，則天徑三十三萬九千四百一里一百二十二步三尺二寸一分七十一分分之九。
value.en: On examination, the ratio is not three to one; with circumference 142 to diameter 45, Heaven's diameter comes to 339,401 li, 122 paces, 3 chi, 2 cun, 1 fen, and 9/71 of a fen.
value.literal: Examined, diameter one is not merely circumference three; with the ratio circumference 142 to diameter 45, Heaven's diameter is 339,401 li, 122 bu, 3 chi, 2 cun, 1 fen, and 9 parts in 71 fen.

value.zh: 以句股法言之，傍萬五千里，句也；
value.en: In right-triangle terms, the 15,000-li horizontal leg is the gou;
value.literal: Speaking in terms of the gou-gu method, the side of 15,000 li is the gou;

value.zh: 立八萬里，股也；
value.en: the 80,000-li vertical leg is the gu;
value.literal: the upright of 80,000 li is the gu;

value.zh: 從日邪射陽城，弦也。
value.en: the slanting ray to Yangcheng is the hypotenuse.
value.literal: from the sun's oblique rays on Yangcheng is the xian.

value.zh: 以句股求弦法入之，得八萬一千三百九十四里三十步五尺三寸六分，天徑之半，而地上去天之數也。
value.en: By the Pythagorean method the hypotenuse comes to 81,394 li, 30 paces, 5 chi, 3 cun, 6 fen—half Heaven's diameter, the height from Earth to the sun.
value.literal: Applying the gou-gu method to find the xian, one obtains 81,394 li, 30 bu, 5 chi, 3 cun, 6 fen—half Heaven's diameter, and the number of li from the ground up to Heaven.

value.zh: 倍之，得十六萬二千七百八十八里六十一步四尺七寸二分，天徑之數也。
value.en: Doubled, that gives 162,788 li, 61 paces, 4 chi, 7 cun, 2 fen for Heaven's full diameter.
value.literal: Doubled, this yields 162,788 li, 61 bu, 4 chi, 7 cun, 2 fen—the number of Heaven's diameter.

value.zh: 以周率乘之，徑率約之，得五十一萬三千六百八十七里六十八步一尺八寸二分，周天之數也。
value.en: Multiplying by pi and reducing by the diameter ratio yields 513,687 li, 68 paces, 1 chi, 8 cun, 2 fen for Heaven's circumference.
value.literal: Multiplying by the circumference ratio and reducing by the diameter ratio, one obtains 513,687 li, 68 bu, 1 chi, 8 cun, 2 fen—the number of Heaven's circuit.

value.zh: 減《甄耀度》、《考異郵》五十五萬七千三百一十二里有奇。
value.en: That is 557,312-odd li less than the figures in those two texts.
value.literal: This is 557,312 and a fraction li less than the Radiance of Degrees and Examination of Strange Correspondences.

value.zh: 一度凡千四百六里百二十四步六寸四分十萬七千五百六十五分分之萬九千三十九，減舊度千五百二十五里二百五十六步三尺三寸二十一萬五千一百三十分分之十六萬七百三十分。
value.en: One degree equals 1,406 li, 124 paces, 6 cun, 4 fen, and 19,039/107,565 of a fen—1,525 li, 256 paces, 3 chi, 3 cun, and 167,030/215,130 of a fen shorter than the older reckoning.
value.literal: One degree totals 1,406 li, 124 bu, 6 cun, 4 fen, and 19,039 parts in 107,565 fen—1,525 li, 256 bu, 3 chi, 3 cun, and 167,030 parts in 215,130 fen less than the old degree.

value.zh: 黃赤二道，相與交錯，其間相去二十四度。
value.en: The ecliptic and equator cross at an angle of 24 degrees.
value.literal: The Yellow and Red roads cross each other; the distance between them is 24 degrees.

value.zh: 以兩儀推之，二道俱三百六十五度有奇，是以知天體圓如彈丸。
value.en: Both circles measure 365-odd degrees by the two-armillary method—proof that Heaven is a perfect sphere.
value.literal: Deducing from the two markers, both roads are 365 and a fraction degrees—hence we know Heaven's body is round like a pellet.

value.zh: 而陸績造渾象，其形如鳥卵，然則黃道應長於赤道矣。
value.en: Yet Lu Ji's globe was egg-shaped, which would make the ecliptic longer than the equator.
value.literal: Yet Lu Ji made a armillary globe whose form is like a bird's egg—then the Yellow Road ought to be longer than the Red Road.

value.zh: 績云天東西南北徑三十五萬七千里，然則績亦以天形正圓也。
value.en: Lu Ji gave Heaven a diameter of 357,000 li, so he too treated the sky as a true sphere.
value.literal: Ji said Heaven's diameter east-west and north-south is 357,000 li—thus Ji also held Heaven's form to be perfectly round.

value.zh: 而渾象為鳥卵，則為自相違背。
value.en: An egg-shaped globe contradicts that assumption.
value.literal: Yet the armillary globe is a bird's egg—this contradicts itself.

value.zh: 史臣案：設器象，定其恆度，合之則吉，失之則凶，以之占察，有何不可。
value.en: The historiographer notes: A model with fixed degrees that match heaven brings good fortune and mismatch brings ill—why should observation be impossible?
value.literal: The historiographer comments: Set up an instrument's image, fix its constant degrees—when they match, auspicious; when they miss, inauspicious; to use it for observation and divination—what could be impossible?

value.zh: 渾文廢絕，故有宣、蓋之論，其術並疏，故後人莫述。
value.en: With Huntian texts lost, Xuanye and Gaitian theories survived, but both are crude and later scholars abandoned them.
value.literal: Huntian texts were abandoned and lost, hence there are Xuanye and Gaitian theories; their methods are all loose, hence later men do not expound them.

value.zh: 揚雄《法言》云：「或人問渾天於雄。
value.en: Yang Xiong's Fayan records: "Someone asked him about Huntian.
value.literal: Yang Xiong's Fayan says: "Someone asked Xiong about Huntian.

value.zh: 雄曰：'落下閎營之，鮮于妄人度之，耿中丞象之，幾乎莫之違也'。」
value.en: He answered: 'Luo Xiahong designed it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, Censor Geng modeled it—hardly a point of dispute.'"
value.literal: Xiong said: 'Luo Xiahong planned it, Xianyu Wangren measured it, Censor-in-Chief Geng modeled it—almost nothing contradicts it.'"

value.zh: 若問天形定體，渾儀疏密，則雄應以渾儀答之，而舉此三人以對者，則知此三人製造渾儀，以圖晷緯。
value.en: Had the question been Heaven's shape or the instrument's scale, he would have described the armillary itself; naming these three men shows they built it to map the gnomon shadow and the celestial warp.
value.literal: If one asked about Heaven's fixed form or the armillary's density, Xiong should have answered with the armillary; yet he named these three men in reply—hence we know these three made the armillary to chart the gnomon and the warp.

value.zh: 問者蓋渾儀之疏密，非問渾儀之淺深也。
value.en: The question concerned the instrument's precision, not cosmological depth.
value.literal: The questioner was probably asking about the armillary's density, not the armillary's depth.

value.zh: 以此而推，則西漢長安已有其器矣。
value.en: On this basis the armillary existed in Western Han Chang'an.
value.literal: Deducing from this, Western Han Chang'an already had this instrument.

value.zh: 將由喪亂亡失，故衡復鑄之乎？
value.en: Did Zhang Heng recast it only because war had destroyed the original?
value.literal: Was it because turmoil and loss destroyed it, that Heng recast it?

value.zh: 王蕃又記古渾儀尺度並張衡改制之文，則知斯器非衡始造，明矣。
value.en: Wang Fan's record of earlier dimensions and Zhang Heng's redesign proves Heng did not invent the armillary.
value.literal: Wang Fan also recorded the ancient armillary's dimensions and the text of Zhang Heng's remaking—hence we know clearly this instrument was not first made by Heng.

value.zh: 衡所造渾儀，傳至魏、晉，中華覆敗，沈沒戎虜；
value.en: Heng's armillary passed to Wei and Jin, then was lost when China fell to the barbarians;
value.literal: The armillary Heng made was transmitted to Wei and Jin; China fell in ruin and sank among the barbarians;

value.zh: 績、蕃舊器，亦不復存。
value.en: and the globes of Lu Ji and Wang Fan vanished as well.
value.literal: the old instruments of Ji and Fan also no longer survive.

value.zh: 晉安帝義熙十四年，高祖平長安，得衡舊器，儀狀雖舉，不綴經星七曜。
value.en: In Yixi year 14 the High Ancestor took Chang'an and recovered Heng's armillary, but its fixed stars and planets no longer aligned.
value.literal: In the fourteenth year of Emperor An's Yixi era, the High Ancestor pacified Chang'an and obtained Heng's old instrument; though its form was raised, it did not link the fixed stars and seven luminaries.

value.en: Great ministers and noble kin all felt themselves estranged and showed discontent on their faces.
value.literal: great ministers noble kin all considered estranged themselves, resentful had discontented expressions.

value.zh: 帝使給事黃門侍郎陸覬私諭之曰：「至尊但欲廣知古事，詢訪前世法式耳，終不親彼而相疏也。」
value.en: The emperor had Supervisor Lu Guan privately instruct them, saying, "His Majesty only wishes to broaden his knowledge of antiquity and inquire into institutions of former ages—that is all; he will never favor them and distance you."
value.literal: emperor made Supervisor Lu Guan privately instruct them said: "Sovereign only wishes broaden knowledge ancient matters, inquire former ages institutions, that is all, ultimately will not favor them and estrange you."

value.en: The crowd's resentment gradually eased.
value.literal: crowd's resentment then slightly eased.
